what: Dollar General runs nearly 21,000 small discount stores, mostly in rural and small-town America where it is often the only general store within miles. Most of what it sells is food and household consumables.
customers: Lower-income households in the southern, midwestern and eastern United States, plus a small operation in Mexico.
money: food, cleaning products, paper goods and tobacco
household goods, clothing and seasonal items
moat: Store locations in places too small for a supermarket, which makes it the convenient option rather than the cheapest, with a supply chain built for small-format stores.
risks: Its core customer is under pressure from inflation and reduced food assistance
Operating margin of 5% is thin and has fallen
Theft and inventory loss have been a persistent problem
opportunities: A back-to-basics programme on store standards and stock availability has improved sales
Lower-income customers trading down from supermarkets benefits it in a weak economy
watch: Same-store sales and gross margin after shrink.
